reason: Both open with a safe 'stop using it, don't keep resetting' message and escalate to an electrician or appliance engineer, but Conversation 1 stops there with a bare one-liner (and tells the owner to 'unplug' a built-in hob) without gathering a single fact. Conversation 2 asks sensible questions about boil-overs and zone pattern, surfaces the electrical smell and the two-zones-on-high load pattern, and then correctly advises isolating at the consumer unit and calling an electrician/engineer with no part recommendation. Its weaknesses are overconfidence ('almost always' earth leak, 'probably' moisture tracking) when overload is still a live possibility, and neither conversation asked which device trips, but Conversation 2 still gave the homeowner far more useful, honest guidance.
